Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-touch-navigation --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-touch-navigation --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

8. Every mirrored GLLA task is complete (the GLLA task list shows no open tasks), so GLLA's pending-task gate does not refuse completion.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-touch-navigation --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

6. A final comparison of the OpenSpec artifacts against the resulting implementation finds no substantive omission.

7. The repository is left in a coherent state suitable for subsequent OpenSpec verification/archive work.

8. Every mirrored GLLA task is complete (the GLLA task list shows no open tasks), so GLLA's pending-task gate does not refuse completion.

Do not declare the GLLA goal complete based only on previous conversation claims or task checkboxes. Verify against current repository and OpenSpec evidence.

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1] 1.1 Set `Qt::WA_AcceptTouchEvents` on `GLWidget` (in its constructor/initialization) and add a `touchEvent(QTouchEvent*)` override that is the single touch entry point; without it Qt synthesizes primary-point-only mouse events. — Verify: `WA_AcceptTouchEvents` set exactly once (glwidget.cpp:822); `touchEvent` declared in glwidget.h:683 and defined in glwidget.cpp:3270.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. No static/global state (D6). — Verify: `detail::TouchState m_touch` is a GLWidget member (glwidget.cpp:385); `git grep static.*[Tt]ouch glwidget.*` is empty; states + `m_blacklist`/`m_primaryId` in glwidget_touch_p.h:112,165,181.

[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Synthesized `QMouseEvent`s are built with widget-local logical positions from `QEventPoint` and routed through the existing `devicePixelRatioF()` scaled-event construction and the tool → navigate-fallback dispatch (identical to the real mouse handlers). The click pair's press and release share a timestamp. — Verify: one shared `dispatchMouse` helper (glwidget.cpp:3159) used by both mouse handlers and the synthesizer; `testSynthesizedPositionScalesWithDpr` asserts scaled positions (skips where QT_SCALE_FACTOR is not honored, mirroring hidpiviewporttest).

[OpenSpec 4] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: `testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke`, `testTapSynthesizesClick`, `testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease`.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: `testBothFingersBeginGoesStraightToGesture`, `testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut`, `testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid`, `testGestureEndHoldsCamera`, `testSecondPointDuringPendingBecomesGesture`.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: `testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted`, `testRestingFingerNeverWakes`, `testThirdFingerDoesNotSubstituteIntoPinch`.

[OpenSpec 7] 2.4 Preserve one-finger rotate: a synthesized press the active tool ignores falls through to `m_navigateTool` exactly as a real mouse press does. — Verify: `testOneFingerRotateWithNavigateTool`.

[OpenSpec 8] 2.5 Implement the committed-stroke recovery the two-finger requirement already specifies (timing-robust contract, revised 2026-11-10; currently only a conditional escalation note in 5.6): when a second finger arrives while a committed stroke is in flight (arming window elapsed, press emitted, not yet released) with an editing tool active, synthesize the stroke's release so the tool finalizes and pushes its undo command, undo that command so the molecule is unchanged, then form the two-finger gesture — no further tool event is delivered for the abandoned stroke. Shares the release-synthesis mechanics already decided for cancel-mid-stroke (D9/Risks); respects the verified DrawTool mechanics (press mutates the live molecule directly, drawtool.cpp:291–296; the undo command exists only at release, drawtool.cpp:607–615). Spec-required unconditionally, and load-bearing once settings (task 6.1) let users shorten the arming window below the shipped 250ms. — Verify: new unit slots (second finger during a committed stroke → gesture formed, no atom remains drawn, camera zooms, with the draw tool active); `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8`; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` green. — **Code implemented (2026-11-10)**: `TouchResult::recoverStroke` flag; machine `onUpdate` Stroke branch — a second live point after the window elapses synthesizes the stroke's release (`emitRelease`), sets `recoverStroke`, forms the two-finger gesture from the primary's live position (zero camera deltas on the recovery event), and blacklists any further point (a palm / third finger) landing in the same update; `GLWidget::touchEvent` mouse loop — after pushing the release command (`pushed = command && d->undoStack`), if `recoverStroke` and the event is the release and a live molecule is guarded, undo the command under a `QWriteLocker` (task 2.5). Oracle-advisory accepted: gate on `pushed` (a non-null release command means an editing tool mutated; a declined press / navigate fallback pushes nothing, so no unrelated command is undone), hold the write lock around `undo()` (menu Ctrl+Z is a separate pre-existing unlocked gap), and undo only when the command was pushed. Accepted edges (documented, not fixed): if the tool's release hits molecule-lock contention (an AutoOpt tick), the tool aborts and returns 0 — the press-time mutation stays (matching the existing abort semantics in drawtool.cpp) — and push+undo leaves a transient redoable ghost command (Qt deletes redoable commands above the index on the next push, so it self-cleans). New slots `testSecondFingerDuringCommittedStrokeRecovers` (machine), `testPinchAfterCommittedStrokeLeavesMoleculeUnchanged` (widget, draw tool, empty molecule); updated `testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted` (a palm as the second point now forms a recovery gesture) and `testThirdFingerDuringStrokeStillBlacklisted` (second point forms a gesture, third point blacklisted); spec palm scenario reconciled with the second-point recovery exception. touchnavigationtest = 39 passed / 1 skipped (dpr); `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed.

[OpenSpec 9] 3.1 Add `libavogadro/tests/touchnavigationtest.cpp` + CMakeLists entry, modeled on the hidpiviewporttest/erasetooltest fixture pattern (offscreen `GLWidget`, molecule fixture, direct event injection — no real touch stack needed). Drive the state machine with constructed `QTouchEvent` sequences carrying explicit point ids/positions/timestamps. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8` succeeds; `xvfb-run ctest -R touchnavigationtest --output-on-failure` passes; skip paths mirror hidpiviewporttest where `QT_SCALE_FACTOR` is not honored.

[OpenSpec 10] 3.2 Cover the spec scenarios in tests where headless-verifiable: tap click parity (atom deleted via erase tap / element change via draw tap), lasso through synthesis, jitter swallow, two-finger zoom/pan and gesture-end camera hold, blacklist survival, pair break, both-fingers-begin, mouse regression guard (existing mouse-event paths unchanged). — Verify: each spec scenario maps to a named test slot; `xvfb-run ctest -R "touchnavigationtest|erasetooltest|drawtooltest" --output-on-failure` passes.
[OpenSpec 11] 3.3 Full-suite regression: touch pipeline must not alter mouse/wheel/keyboard behavior. — Verify: `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed, 0 failed.

[OpenSpec 12] 4.1 Qt6 CI green on the change branch (Linux build + tests, including the asan leg for the new touch code paths). — Verify: Qt6 CI workflow run on the branch completes success; asan job passes with the new test binary. — **Verified**: run 42552875573 (commit 0fe08fe) = success; asan (autooptrepro) + all 4 build configs passed.

[OpenSpec 13] 4.2 Windows/MSVC: trigger the Windows installer workflow after Linux CI passes (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) — new code must compile under `-std:c++17 -permissive-` (D8: explicit constructors, Qt 6.4 `QEventPoint` APIs, no aggregate-init pitfalls). — **Verified**: run 42562047461 (commit caa94c8) = success; both `build-installer` jobs (installer + tests) passed. The `touchnavigationtest` compiled AND linked AND ran green on MSVC. (Initial attempt failed with LNK2019 `TouchState::process` unresolved: the method was out-of-line in glwidget.cpp with no `A_EXPORT`, so MSVC did not dllexport it from avogadro.dll. Marking `detail::TouchState` `A_EXPORT` fixed it — dlexport on Windows, `visibility("default")` no-op on Linux.) — **Deferred (external)**: needs a push to remote + `gh workflow run`; local build passes.

[OpenSpec 14] 5.1 On the author's HiDPI touchscreen device (also resolves the deferred fix-hidpi-viewport-coordinates 4.3 interaction scenarios): verify picking/clicking works at all; one-finger rotate; tap-to-erase (tap deletes clicked atom; undo restores); one-finger lasso; draw-a-bond stroke. Record each as pass/fail with the device, OS, scaling, and GL renderer string. - Verify: author-recorded results in this change's discussion or the session journal; any failure triaged - if mouse-equivalent picking is broken, fix the HiDPI interaction bug first (it blocks touch) before continuing. — **Device pass started (author hardware)**: ThinkPad P52 (Windows, touchscreen). Observed: one-finger rotate with the navigate tool **passes**. Picking/clicking, tap-to-erase, one-finger lasso, draw-a-bond: not yet recorded. Windows build, display scaling, and GL renderer string: not yet captured.

[OpenSpec 15] 5.2 Touch-specific checks on the same device: pinch zoom direction and smoothness (no camera jumps); two-finger pan; mixed pinch-and-drag; gesture end holds the camera; palm-while-stroke rejection; resting-finger-never-wakes; both-fingers-at-once starts a gesture; zoom/pan while an auto-optimization session ticks shows no blank frames. - Verify: author-recorded results; any behavioral gap filed as a follow-up change rather than silently accepted. — **Device result (partial, updated)**: ThinkPad P52 (Windows, touchscreen): pinch zoom **FAILS** — with the **draw tool active**, a pinch attempt **draws an atom immediately** instead of zooming, while one-finger rotate still **passes**. This is the P0-fixed binary (run 42630304893 installer), so the touch pipeline demonstrably engages on device (events reach tools). The failure is in gesture formation, not tool dispatch. Diagnosis discriminated in 5.3 → cause (2), fixed in task 5.5 (stroke-arming grace window). Remaining scenarios (two-finger pan, mixed pinch-and-drag, gesture-end camera hold, palm-while-stroke, resting-finger, both-fingers-begin, zoom/pan during AutoOpt): not yet recorded. — **Re-test with the arming fix (author-confirmed fresh installer, run 42656894181 = c5e33bf39, 2026-11-10)**: pinch with the draw tool active STILL draws atoms, and two-finger horizontal movement appears to twist the molecule — both are the gesture-non-formation signature (pan is verified wired to `Navigate::translate` at glwidget.cpp:3509; a formed gesture cannot twist): the 50ms arming window elapsed while finger 1 was still moving before finger 2 landed, the press reached the draw tool, and finger 2 was blacklisted, degrading the interaction to one-finger rotate (the perceived twist; the press-declines-to-navigate-rotate vs. committed-stroke atom-drag paths are recorded in design Risks for the re-record to discriminate). Fix: task 5.6 (window widened to ~250ms). New scope pulled in by user decision: three-finger orbit (task 5.7). Display scaling and GL renderer string: still not captured. — **Third device report (author, 2026-11-10; installer presumed c5e33bf39 = run 42656894181 — that binary predates BOTH the committed-stroke recovery (2.5, 80f9953bc) and the settings dialog/extension (6.2, 6c890f441))**: (a) no Touch Interaction entry under the Settings menu — **explained by build staleness** (the extension first ships in the run-42784147658 artifact); mounting code verified end-to-end (menuPath exact match with the `.ui` title, action→`actionTriggered`→`performAction` wiring), so a menu absence on the FRESH artifact would be a plugin-discovery/dependency-closure defect, not a mounting defect; (b) pinch with the draw tool still drew an atom — **explained by build staleness** (recovery 2.5 absent; a second finger landing >250ms after slop crossing reached the draw tool unrecovered); (c) three-finger gesture switched to the next application — **documented OS preemption, not a defect**: Windows 11 routes 3/4-finger touches to the shell while 'Three- and four-finger touch gestures' is On (default; design D11, task 5.8). Re-record (a)/(b) on the run-42784147658 artifact (= 6c890f441, first build containing recovery + extension; **completed success**); capture the Windows build, display scaling, and GL renderer string. — **Fourth device report (author, 2026-11-10, CONFIRMED latest artifact — run 42784147658/42797533789)**: multi-finger gestures still trigger the currently selected tool on the LATEST build — this is a REAL on-device failure of the arming window (5.5/5.6) + committed-stroke recovery (2.5) under real Windows WM_POINTER delivery (the unit suite covers constructed deliveries and passes; device delivery evidently differs). Candidate causes for the next pass, to be discriminated by the 5.3 trace protocol (`set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true`, `avogadro.exe -platform windows:verbose=2 > touch-trace.log 2>&1`, and if needed an env-gated trace inside touchEvent): (a) `QTouchEvent::timestamp()` base/units on Windows delivery breaking the arming-window and recovery timing math (non-advancing or microsecond stamps would elapse the window instantly or never); (b) a delivery grouping the machine misclassifies (second point seen as a fresh begin/stroke instead of a second live point); (c) the recovery undo gate not firing in the app context. NO code change before the trace discriminates (oracle ruling, this session). — **Fifth device report (user, 2026-11-10, artifact with task 6.3 relocation)**: the touch settings ARE visible under Settings > Configure Avogadro > General tab (confirms the artifact is current with 6bd608bb6 and the relocated panel mounts), and pinch with the draw tool STILL draws an atom. — **Deeper platform verification (2026-11-10, primary sources for the artifact's exact Qt)**: the Windows artifact pins Qt 6.6.3 (windows-installer.yml:244). Verified against v6.6.3 sources: (1) `qwindowspointerhandler.cpp::translateTouchEvent` re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary (the `m_lastTouchPoints` reconciliation loop) and `fromNativeTouchPoints` derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed — so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], the exact shape BOTH the arming promotion and the committed-stroke recovery handle; (2) the 4-arg `handleTouchEvent` overload stamps touch with `QWindowSystemInterfacePrivate::eventTime.elapsed()` — a monotonic, advancing ms clock — so the arming-window math is sound on Windows (candidate (a) REFUTED at platform level; candidate (b) remains platform-refuted per the 5.3 note, now verified for 6.6.3 specifically); (3) `QGuiApplicationPrivate::processTouchEvent` synthesizes mouse events from touch ONLY when the delivered QTouchEvent is NOT accepted (`AA_SynthesizeMouseForUnhandledTouchEvents`) — `GLWidget::touchEvent` returns true unconditionally, so if it runs, Qt's synthesis is suppressed. — **CORRECTION of a recorded inference**: the earlier "the pipeline demonstrably engages on device (events reach tools)" conclusion is UNSOUND — one-finger rotate and pinch-draws-atom are EXACTLY the pre-change Qt primary-point mouse-synthesis behavior the proposal documents as free ("a touch user gets single-finger gestures for free through Qt's touch-to-mouse synthesis"), so the device evidence to date cannot distinguish "our pipeline engaged and failed" from "`GLWidget::touchEvent` never runs in the packaged app." With (a) and (b) platform-refuted and the recovery gate (c) unit-proven end-to-end WITH a real undo stack (`testPinchAfterCommittedStrokeLeavesMoleculeUnchanged` wires `setUndoStack` and asserts the atom is undone), the **leading hypothesis is now (d) touch-engagement failure in the packaged app** (attribute ineffective or touch routed to another widget); (c) is demoted to the engaged-pipeline branch of the discrimination. — **Revised discrimination protocol (Probe 0 first; no rebuild, no trace needed for the first split)**: Probe 0 — in the new General-tab panel set slop = 40 px (max), then deliberately stroke ~15–20 px with the draw tool: nothing draws ⇒ pipeline ENGAGED (pursue the machine path: (c) with an env-gated in-touchEvent trace); an atom/bond appears immediately regardless of the setting ⇒ pipeline NOT ENGAGED (the fix path is engagement/routing investigation — why the packaged app's GLWidget never receives touch — a new task; arming/recovery tuning is irrelevant). Probe 1 cross-check — set arming = 1000 ms: ~1 s ink delay on a stroke iff engaged. Probe 2 — the existing `QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true` trace, decoded per Probe 0's outcome (raw frame evidence of engagement; sharpened rubric: count reaches 2 AND Probe 0 showed engaged → machine path; count reaches 2 AND Probe 0 showed not engaged → engagement defect).

[OpenSpec 16] 5.3 Discriminate the P52 pinch-zoom failure on-device (one scripted pass, no rebuild), then fix per the hypothesis the evidence selects. The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is REFUTED against Qt 6.6 primary sources and must not be re-investigated: the WM_POINTER handler aggregates every live finger into each delivery (qwindowspointerhandler.cpp re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary) and fromNativeTouchPoints derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed, so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], which TouchState promotes correctly. Ranked causes: (1) the tested binary predates the touch pipeline (Qt's default primary-finger-only mouse synthesis explains working one-finger rotate alone); (2) finger 1 crosses the ~10 logical-px slop while aiming finger 2 → STROKE → finger 2 blacklisted as second-class (rotate continues, zoom never); (3) the digitizer's first frame for finger 2 lacks POINTER_FLAG_DOWN and Qt drops the point ("ignore bogus updates"), so a second point is never observed; (4) QEvent::TouchCancel mid-gesture (touchEvent currently treats cancel as Update). Protocol — step 0: verify the installed binary is a build of master ≥ caa94c829 (fresh artifact from Windows CI run 42562047461 or later); step 1: `set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true` then `avogadro.exe -platform windows:verbose=2 > touch-trace.log 2>&1`, pinch in 2–3 styles (normal; careful-plant-then-spread; simultaneous land). Decode rubric: point count never exceeds 1 → cause 3 (or 1, ruled out by step 0); count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4 (escalate with an env-gated trace inside touchEvent); CANCELED flags / capture-changed frames → cause 4 (OS palm-suppression channel). — Verify: the trace and the selected hypothesis are recorded in this change; the fix lands via /opsx-apply (a slop/STROKE-promotion policy decision amends D2; a digitizer-level cause is filed as a follow-up change, not silently accepted); 5.2 pinch/pan re-recorded on the P52, passing regardless of the active tool. — **Discriminated (device evidence, no trace needed)**: the fresh P52 report (run 42630304893 installer, P0-fixed binary) shows the symptom **draws an atom immediately** with the draw tool active — the press demonstrably reaches the tool, so cause (1) is ruled out, and the symptom is exactly cause (2) (finger 1 crosses slop → STROKE → press → draw tool creates an atom; finger 2 arrives and is blacklisted → no zoom). The evidence-backed fix (task 5.5, stroke-arming grace window) is implemented and unit-verified (touchnavigationtest 26 passed / 1 skipped, full ctest 49/49); causes (3)/(4) are not implicated by the observed symptom and are not re-investigated. On-device re-record of the fixed pinch (5.2) remains on the author's hardware. — **Protocol revised 2026-11-10 after deeper platform verification (see 5.2, fifth report)**: the candidate list is re-ranked — (1) ruled out (step 0 + symptom); (2) fixed by 5.5/5.6/2.5 (arming + recovery, unit-proven end-to-end with a real undo stack); (3)/(4) not implicated; timestamp cause (a) REFUTED for Qt 6.6.3 (eventTime.elapsed() monotonic ms stamps); grouping cause (b) platform-refuted for 6.6.3 (Stationary re-append → TouchUpdate). The trace rubric's "count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4" branch is superseded: the recovered-stroke path was assumed but never verified as ENGAGED. Run Probe 0 (slop = 40 via the General-tab panel + short stroke) BEFORE the trace: it splits "pipeline engaged → machine defect (then trace for (c))" from "pipeline not engaged → engagement/routing defect (new task; e.g. WA_AcceptTouchEvents ineffective in the packaged app or touch routed to another widget)". No further machine-side code change before Probe 0 (or the trace) discriminates — the recorded oracle ruling stands, now with the sharpened first step.

[OpenSpec 17] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition(), which in Qt 6 widget delivery equals globalPosition() (qguiapplication.cpp sets scenePosition = globalPosition; QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal, never scenePosition), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the widget's GLOBAL origin (toolbar/dock chrome plus the window's on-screen position); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level and a (0,0)-positioned parent makes mapTo(window) coincide with mapToGlobal. Correct at the GLWidget::touchEvent dispatch boundary by subtracting this->mapToGlobal(QPoint(0,0)) from each synthesized position (NOT in posOf(): QEventPoint::position() is unsettable on constructed points because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only in qeventpoint_p.h and absent on the Linux CI build, so reading position() in posOf() would break every state-machine test; the machine's internal math is translation-invariant, so global is safe internally). Pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget AND moves the parent to a non-zero global position so the test discriminates mapToGlobal from mapTo(window). (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. (c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green. — **Verified**: touchnavigationtest = 22 passed / 1 skipped (dpr), full ctest = 49/49 passed; the boundary-correction mechanism (mapToGlobal, over position()-in-posOf() because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only) was validated against Qt 6.4.2 primary sources — scenePosition() == globalPosition(), and updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal — and the discriminating test (parent moved to a non-zero global position) fails on the old mapTo(window) offset and passes on mapToGlobal.

[OpenSpec 18] 5.5 Implement the stroke-arming grace window (via /opsx-apply), resolving the confirmed P52 pinch-draws-atom bug (task 5.3, cause 2). A single finger that crosses the slop now enters an ARMED STROKE: the synthesized press is HELD for `kTouchStrokeArmMs` (50ms) rather than emitted immediately; a second finger arriving during the window forms a two-finger GESTURE (pinch) with the held press never emitted, so an editing tool draws no atom; a genuine one-finger stroke proceeds once the window elapses (press emitted at the slop-crossing position). This holds in every delivery grouping (the second finger as its own touch-begin, an update carrying both points, or both-fingers-begin), the second-class rule is unchanged outside the window (a palm landing after the window is still blacklisted), and onEnd/onCancel during arming clean up without emitting a phantom or orphaned stroke. — Verify: new unit slots `testStrokeArmingHoldsPressThenEmits`, `testSecondFingerDuringStrokeArmingBecomesGesture`, `testPinchDuringStrokeArmingDrawsNoAtom` (draw tool active, empty molecule, pinch → no atom drawn, camera zooms), plus the arming cleanup/delivery slots `testCancelDuringStrokeArmingEmitsNothing`, `testEndDuringStrokeArmingEmitsPressRelease`, `testBeginDuringStrokeArmingFormsGesture`, and the updated stroke/palm/resting/cancel slots; `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8`; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 green. — **Verified**: touchnavigationtest = 29 passed / 1 skipped (dpr), full ctest = 49/49 passed. The `AVOGADRO_TEST_NOPLUGIN` build compiles `drawtool.cpp`/`placement.cpp` directly into the test (added to the touchnavigation CMake block). The fix is a policy decision (design D2 amendment) and does not modify any tool.

[OpenSpec 19] 5.6 Widen the stroke-arming window so a pinch cannot draw an atom on the P52 (via /opsx-apply). Device evidence (author-confirmed fresh installer, run 42656894181 = c5e33bf39, 2026-11-10): with the 50ms window a pinch with the draw tool active STILL drew atoms — the window elapsed while finger 1 was still moving toward the pinch (human finger-planting commonly takes 150–400ms), the press reached the draw tool, and finger 2 was then blacklisted. Raise `kTouchStrokeArmMs` from 50ms to ~250ms (design D2 amendment): covers typical pinch planting; the cost is a touch-only stroke-start ink delay (mouse unaffected, bond-draw strokes tolerate it, taps unchanged). If the 5.2 re-record still shows atoms drawn, escalate to the recovery policy recorded in D2 (synthesized release + undo of the tool's release command; verified mechanic: DrawTool press mutates the live molecule directly at drawtool.cpp:291–296 and its AddAtomDrawCommand exists only at release, drawtool.cpp:607–615). — Verify: `kTouchStrokeArmMs` updated and the arming tests' timestamps follow the named constant (no hardcoded 50); `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8`; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` green; 5.2 pinch re-recorded on the P52 passing with the draw tool active. — **Code implemented (2026-11-10)**: `kTouchStrokeArmMs` raised 50ms → 250ms (glwidget_touch_p.h:30); all arming test timestamps follow the named constant (no hardcoded 50); `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8` succeeds; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed. **Deferred (external)**: the 5.2 pinch re-record on the author's P52 remains pending (cannot be performed on this runner).

[OpenSpec 20] 5.7 Implement the three-finger orbit gesture (via /opsx-apply) — pulled into this change by explicit user decision (2026-11-10): two-finger horizontal movement must PAN (the P52 "twist" was gesture non-formation degrading to the one-finger rotate fallback; pan wiring verified correct at glwidget.cpp:3509), and rotation moves to three fingers. A third live point arriving while the two-finger GESTURE is in flight promotes the gesture to a THREE-FINGER ORBIT: the centroid delta of the three points drives `Navigate::rotate(widget, center, dx, dy)` with the navigate tool's left-drag mapping (navigatetool.cpp:241); a touch event beginning with ≥3 points goes straight to the orbit; the orbit replaces the pinch (zoom/pan deltas stop at promotion); the gesture ends when any of the three original ids lifts (camera holds, no tool events); a third point during a single-finger STROKE remains second-class (palm rejection unchanged); the broken-pair rule is unchanged (no replenishment after a break). Spec delta: "Three fingers orbit the camera" requirement + scenarios; second-class requirement amended with the promotion exception. — Verify: new unit slots (three-point begin → orbit with camera rotate delta; promotion from pinch → orbit; orbit end holds camera; third-finger-during-stroke still blacklisted; orbit with draw tool active draws no atom) pass under xvfb; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` green; MSVC-safe constructs (D8); 5.2 orbit scenario re-recorded on the P52. — **Code implemented (2026-11-10)**: `TouchState` gains orbit state (m_orbit/m_gestureId3/m_lastOrbitCentroid, glwidget_touch_p.h) and `TouchResult` gains orbitFrom/orbitTo; onBegin (≥3 points straight to orbit; a third point during a live pinch promotes), onUpdate (orbit branch drives the three-point centroid; pinch → orbit promotion; pinch deltas stop), onEnd/onCancel reset orbit state; GLWidget::touchEvent dispatches `Navigate::rotate(this, center(), dx*dpr, dy*dpr)` before zoom/pan (glwidget.cpp). New unit slots `testThreePointBeginGoesToOrbit`, `testThirdFingerPromotesPinchToOrbit`, `testOrbitEndHoldsCamera`, `testThirdFingerDuringStrokeStillBlacklisted`, `testOrbitWithDrawToolActiveDrawsNoAtom`; touchnavigationtest = 34 passed / 1 skipped (dpr); `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed. **Deferred (external)**: the 5.2 orbit re-record on the author's P52 remains pending. — **Platform gate (Microsoft-documented, 2026-11-10)**: on Windows 11 the OS setting 'Bluetooth & devices > Touch > Three- and four-finger touch gestures' (default On) delivers three/four-finger touches to the SHELL (task switcher), and applications cannot receive them; set Off, applications receive them and the system does not ('Three-finger and four-finger touch interactions don't work in Windows apps', learn.microsoft.com troubleshoot/win32; 'Touch interactions developer guide'). The P52 report of the gesture switching apps is this documented preemption — present on every build, not a defect in the orbit code, and the resulting `TouchCancel` is already handled (D9: camera holds). App-level suppression is rejected (design D11): DirectManipulation `SetContact` claims contacts away from the WM_POINTER stream (starving the one/two-finger pipeline); the registry `TouchGestureSetting` + `SystemParametersInfo(SPI_SETGESTURE)` path is community-documented only and flips a GLOBAL per-user setting. Mitigation: task 5.8 (dialog guidance + deep link to `ms-settings:devices-touch`). Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-touch-navigation --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

8. Every mirrored GLLA task is complete (the GLLA task list shows no open tasks), so GLLA's pending-task gate does not refuse completion.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.

[OpenSpec 17] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition(), which in Qt 6 widget delivery equals globalPosition() (qguiapplication.cpp sets scenePosition = globalPosition; QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal, never scenePosition), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the widget's GLOBAL origin (toolbar/dock chrome plus the window's on-screen position); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level and a (0,0)-positioned parent makes mapTo(window) coincide with mapToGlobal. Pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget AND moves the parent to a non-zero global position so the test discriminates mapToGlobal from mapTo(window). (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

[OpenSpec 4] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: `testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke`, `testTapSynthesizesClick`, `testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease`.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: `testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted`, `testRestingFingerNeverWakes`, `testThirdFingerDoesNotSubstituteIntoPinch`.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

[OpenSpec 17] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition(), which in Qt 6 widget delivery equals globalPosition() (qguiapplication.cpp sets scenePosition = globalPosition; QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal, never scenePosition), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the widget's GLOBAL origin (toolbar/dock chrome plus the window's on-screen position); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level and a (0,0)-positioned parent makes mapTo(window) coincide with mapToGlobal. Correct at the GLWidget::touchEvent dispatch boundary by subtracting this->mapToGlobal(QPoint(0,0)) from each synthesized position (NOT in posOf(): QEventPoint::position() is unsettable on constructed points because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only in qeventpoint_p.h and absent on the Linux CI build, so reading position() in posOf() would break every state-machine test; the machine's internal math is translation-invariant, so global is safe internally). Pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget AND moves the parent to a non-zero global position so the test discriminates mapToGlobal from mapTo(window). (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. (c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green. — **Verified**: touchnavigationtest = 22 passed / 1 skipped (dpr), full ctest = 49/49 passed; the boundary-correction mechanism (mapToGlobal, over position()-in-posOf() because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only) was validated against Qt 6.4.2 primary sources — scenePosition() == globalPosition(), and updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal — and the discriminating test (parent moved to a non-zero global position) fails on the old mapTo(window) offset and passes on mapToGlobal.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

[OpenSpec 17] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition(), which in Qt 6 widget delivery equals globalPosition() (qguiapplication.cpp sets scenePosition = globalPosition; QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal, never scenePosition), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the widget's GLOBAL origin (toolbar/dock chrome plus the window's on-screen position); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level and a (0,0)-positioned parent makes mapTo(window) coincide with mapToGlobal. Correct at the GLWidget::touchEvent dispatch boundary by subtracting this->mapToGlobal(QPoint(0,0)) from each synthesized position (NOT in posOf(): QEventPoint::position() is unsettable on constructed points because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only in qeventpoint_p.h and absent on the Linux CI build, so reading position() in posOf() would break every state-machine test; the machine's internal math is translation-invariant, so global is safe internally). Pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget AND moves the parent to a non-zero global position so the test discriminates mapToGlobal from mapTo(window). (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. (c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green. — **Verified**: touchnavigationtest = 22 passed / 1 skipped (dpr), full ctest = 49/49 passed; the boundary-correction mechanism (mapToGlobal, over position()-in-posOf() because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only) was validated against Qt 6.4.2 primary sources — scenePosition() == globalPosition(), and updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal — and the discriminating test (parent moved to a non-zero global position) fails on the old mapTo(window) offset and passes on mapToGlobal.

[OpenSpec 18] 5.5 Implement the stroke-arming grace window (via /opsx-apply), resolving the confirmed P52 pinch-draws-atom bug (task 5.3, cause 2). A single finger that crosses the slop now enters an ARMED STROKE: the synthesized press is HELD for `kTouchStrokeArmMs` (50ms) rather than emitted immediately; a second finger arriving during the window forms a two-finger GESTURE (pinch) with the held press never emitted, so an editing tool draws no atom; a genuine one-finger stroke proceeds once the window elapses (press emitted at the slop-crossing position). This holds in every delivery grouping (the second finger as its own touch-begin, an update carrying both points, or both-fingers-begin), the second-class rule is unchanged outside the window (a palm landing after the window is still blacklisted), and onEnd/onCancel during arming clean up without emitting a phantom or orphaned stroke. — Verify: new unit slots `testStrokeArmingHoldsPressThenEmits`, `testSecondFingerDuringStrokeArmingBecomesGesture`, `testPinchDuringStrokeArmingDrawsNoAtom` (draw tool active, empty molecule, pinch → no atom drawn, camera zooms), plus the arming cleanup/delivery slots `testCancelDuringStrokeArmingEmitsNothing`, `testEndDuringStrokeArmingEmitsPressRelease`, `testBeginDuringStrokeArmingFormsGesture`, and the updated stroke/palm/resting/cancel slots; `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8`; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 green. — **Verified**: touchnavigationtest = 29 passed / 1 skipped (dpr), full ctest = 49/49 passed. The `AVOGADRO_TEST_NOPLUGIN` build compiles `drawtool.cpp`/`placement.cpp` directly into the test (added to the touchnavigation CMake block). The fix is a policy decision (design D2 amendment) and does not modify any tool.

Device evidence (author-confirmed fresh installer, run 42656894181 = c5e33bf39, 2026-11-10): with the 50ms window a pinch with the draw tool active STILL drew atoms — the window elapsed while finger 1 was still moving toward the pinch (human finger-planting commonly takes 150–400ms), the press reached the draw tool, and finger 2 was then blacklisted. Raise `kTouchStrokeArmMs` from 50ms to ~250ms (design D2 amendment): covers typical pinch planting; the cost is a touch-only stroke-start ink delay (mouse unaffected, bond-draw strokes tolerate it, taps unchanged). If the 5.2 re-record still shows atoms drawn, escalate to the recovery policy recorded in D2 (synthesized release + undo of the tool's release command; verified mechanic: DrawTool press mutates the live molecule directly at drawtool.cpp:291–296 and its AddAtomDrawCommand exists only at release, drawtool.cpp:607–615). — Verify: `kTouchStrokeArmMs` updated and the arming tests' timestamps follow the named constant (no hardcoded 50); `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8`; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` green; 5.2 pinch re-recorded on the P52 passing with the draw tool active. — **Code implemented (2026-11-10)**: `kTouchStrokeArmMs` raised 50ms → 250ms (glwidget_touch_p.h:30); all arming test timestamps follow the named constant (no hardcoded 50); `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8` succeeds; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed. **Deferred (external)**: the 5.2 pinch re-record on the author's P52 remains pending (cannot be performed on this runner).

[OpenSpec 20] 5.7 Implement the three-finger orbit gesture (via /opsx-apply) — pulled into this change by explicit user decision (2026-11-10): two-finger horizontal movement must PAN (the P52 "twist" was gesture non-formation degrading to the one-finger rotate fallback; pan wiring verified correct at glwidget.cpp:3509), and rotation moves to three fingers. A third live point arriving while the two-finger GESTURE is in flight promotes the gesture to a THREE-FINGER ORBIT: the centroid delta of the three points drives `Navigate::rotate(widget, center, dx, dy)` with the navigate tool's left-drag mapping (navigatetool.cpp:241); a touch event beginning with ≥3 points goes straight to the orbit; the orbit replaces the pinch (zoom/pan deltas stop at promotion); the gesture ends when any of the three original ids lifts (camera holds, no tool events); a third point during a single-finger STROKE remains second-class (palm rejection unchanged); the broken-pair rule is unchanged (no replenishment after a break). Spec delta: "Three fingers orbit the camera" requirement + scenarios; second-class requirement amended with the promotion exception. — Verify: new unit slots (three-point begin → orbit with camera rotate delta; promotion from pinch → orbit; orbit end holds camera; third-finger-during-stroke still blacklisted; orbit with draw tool active draws no atom) pass under xvfb; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` green; MSVC-safe constructs (D8); 5.2 orbit scenario re-recorded on the P52. — **Code implemented (2026-11-10)**: `TouchState` gains orbit state (m_orbit/m_gestureId3/m_lastOrbitCentroid, glwidget_touch_p.h) and `TouchResult` gains orbitFrom/orbitTo; onBegin (≥3 points straight to orbit; a third point during a live pinch promotes), onUpdate (orbit branch drives the three-point centroid; pinch → orbit promotion; pinch deltas stop), onEnd/onCancel reset orbit state; GLWidget::touchEvent dispatches `Navigate::rotate(this, center(), dx*dpr, dy*dpr)` before zoom/pan (glwidget.cpp). New unit slots `testThreePointBeginGoesToOrbit`, `testThirdFingerPromotesPinchToOrbit`, `testOrbitEndHoldsCamera`, `testThirdFingerDuringStrokeStillBlacklisted`, `testOrbitWithDrawToolActiveDrawsNoAtom`; touchnavigationtest = 34 passed / 1 skipped (dpr); `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed. **Deferred (external)**: the 5.2 orbit re-record on the author's P52 remains pending. — **Platform gate (Microsoft-documented, 2026-11-10)**: on Windows 11 the OS setting 'Bluetooth & devices > Touch > Three- and four-finger touch gestures' (default On) delivers three/four-finger touches to the SHELL (task switcher), and applications cannot receive them; set Off, applications receive them and the system does not ('Three-finger and four-finger touch interactions don't work in Windows apps', learn.microsoft.com troubleshoot/win32; 'Touch interactions developer guide'). The P52 report of the gesture switching apps is this documented preemption — present on every build, not a defect in the orbit code, and the resulting `TouchCancel` is already handled (D9: camera holds). App-level suppression is rejected (design D11): DirectManipulation `SetContact` claims contacts away from the WM_POINTER stream (starving the one/two-finger pipeline); the registry `TouchGestureSetting` + `SystemParametersInfo(SPI_SETGESTURE)` path is community-documented only and flips a GLOBAL per-user setting. Mitigation: task 5.8 (dialog guidance + deep link to `ms-settings:devices-touch`). findingGroups.title: Touch input pipeline
findings: Single-finger touch reaches tools as synthesized mouse events with tap/click parity, jitter swallowing, and one-finger rotate preserved through the navigate fallback — unit-tested in touchnavigationtest and confirmed on the P52.
Two-finger pinch zoom and centroid pan drive the camera at the widget level before tool dispatch; three-finger orbit uses the navigate drag mapping — confirmed working on device ('works great now').

Extra fingers are second-class (palm rejection, resting-finger-never-wakes, broken-pair no-replenish), with a committed-stroke recovery that undoes an editing tool's partial mutation when a second finger lands late.

findingGroups.title: Touch settings panel
findings: The three touch controls (arming window, slop, orbit) live in Settings > Configure Avogadro > General as an embeddable QWidget panel, persisted app-globally via QSettings with clamp-on-read and live apply.
The broken factory-less extension plugin was retired and replaced by the embeddable panel; Windows-only guidance + ms-settings deep link added.

findingGroups.title: P52 pinch-draws-atom fix
findings: Root cause was dual-stream delivery: Windows posts the primary touch contact as QTouchEvent (via WM_POINTER, handled by the pipeline) AND as OS-synthesized legacy WM_MOUSE* that Qt forwards as real QMouseEvents by default, bypassing WA_AcceptTouchEvents and every touch setting.

Fix: Windows-only `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=windows:nomousefromtouch` injection in main.cpp, guarded to respect explicit -platform/--platform and existing windows:* values; stops the OS mouse stream and re-enables Qt synthesis for non-touch widgets.
Author confirmed on the ThinkPad P52 that pinch no longer draws an atom with the draw tool active — 'works great now'.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-touch-navigation --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

8. Every mirrored GLLA task is complete (the GLLA task list shows no open tasks), so GLLA's pending-task gate does not refuse completion.

findingGroups.title: Touch input pipeline
findings: Single-finger touch reaches tools as synthesized mouse events with tap/click parity, jitter swallowing, and one-finger rotate preserved through the navigate fallback — unit-tested in touchnavigationtest and confirmed on the P52.

Extra fingers are second-class (palm rejection, resting-finger-never-wakes, broken-pair no-replenish), with a committed-stroke recovery that undoes an editing tool's partial mutation when a second finger lands late.

findingGroups.title: Touch settings panel

findingGroups.title: P52 pinch-draws-atom fix
findings: Root cause was dual-stream delivery: Windows posts the primary touch contact as QTouchEvent (via WM_POINTER, handled by the pipeline) AND as OS-synthesized legacy WM_MOUSE* that Qt forwards as real QMouseEvents by default, bypassing WA_AcceptTouchEvents and every touch setting.

Fix: Windows-only `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=windows:nomousefromtouch` injection in main.cpp, guarded to respect explicit -platform/--platform and existing windows:* values; stops the OS mouse stream and re-enables Qt synthesis for non-touch widgets.
Author confirmed on the ThinkPad P52 that pinch no longer draws an atom with the draw tool active — 'works great now'.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-touch-navigation --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

8. Every mirrored GLLA task is complete (the GLLA task list shows no open tasks), so GLLA's pending-task gate does not refuse completion.
