The evidence-backed fix (task 5.5, stroke-arming grace window) is implemented and unit-verified (touchnavigationtest 26 passed / 1 skipped, full ctest 49/49); causes (3)/(4) are not implicated by the observed symptom and are not re-investigated. On-device re-record of the fixed pinch (5.2) remains on the author's hardware. — **Protocol revised 2026-11-10 after deeper platform verification (see 5.2, fifth report)**: the candidate list is re-ranked — (1) ruled out (step 0 + symptom); (2) fixed by 5.5/5.6/2.5 (arming + recovery, unit-proven end-to-end with a real undo stack); (3)/(4) not implicated; timestamp cause (a) REFUTED for Qt 6.6.3 (eventTime.elapsed() monotonic ms stamps); grouping cause (b) platform-refuted for 6.6.3 (Stationary re-append → TouchUpdate). The trace rubric's "count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4" branch is superseded: the recovered-stroke path was assumed but never verified as ENGAGED. Run Probe 0 (slop = 40 via the General-tab panel + short stroke) BEFORE the trace: it splits "pipeline engaged → machine defect (then trace for (c))" from "pipeline not engaged → engagement/routing defect (new task; e.g. WA_AcceptTouchEvents ineffective in the packaged app or touch routed to another widget)". No further machine-side code change before Probe 0 (or the trace) discriminates — the recorded oracle ruling stands, now with the sharpened first step.

[OpenSpec 17] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition(), which in Qt 6 widget delivery equals globalPosition() (qguiapplication.cpp sets scenePosition = globalPosition; QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal, never scenePosition), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the widget's GLOBAL origin (toolbar/dock chrome plus the window's on-screen position); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level and a (0,0)-positioned parent makes mapTo(window) coincide with mapToGlobal. Correct at the GLWidget::touchEvent dispatch boundary by subtracting this->mapToGlobal(QPoint(0,0)) from each synthesized position (NOT in posOf(): QEventPoint::position() is unsettable on constructed points because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only in qeventpoint_p.h and absent on the Linux CI build, so reading position() in posOf() would break every state-machine test; the machine's internal math is translation-invariant, so global is safe internally). Pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget AND moves the parent to a non-zero global position so the test discriminates mapToGlobal from mapTo(window). (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. (c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green. — **Verified**: touchnavigationtest = 22 passed / 1 skipped (dpr), full ctest = 49/49 passed; the boundary-correction mechanism (mapToGlobal, over position()-in-posOf() because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only) was validated against Qt 6.4.2 primary sources — scenePosition() == globalPosition(), and updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal — and the discriminating test (parent moved to a non-zero global position) fails on the old mapTo(window) offset and passes on mapToGlobal.

[OpenSpec 18] 5.5 Implement the stroke-arming grace window (via /opsx-apply), resolving the confirmed P52 pinch-draws-atom bug (task 5.3, cause 2). A single finger that crosses the slop now enters an ARMED STROKE: the synthesized press is HELD for `kTouchStrokeArmMs` (50ms) rather than emitted immediately; a second finger arriving during the window forms a two-finger GESTURE (pinch) with the held press never emitted, so an editing tool draws no atom; a genuine one-finger stroke proceeds once the window elapses (press emitted at the slop-crossing position). This holds in every delivery grouping (the second finger as its own touch-begin, an update carrying both points, or both-fingers-begin), the second-class rule is unchanged outside the window (a palm landing after the window is still blacklisted), and onEnd/onCancel during arming clean up without emitting a phantom or orphaned stroke. — Verify: new unit slots `testStrokeArmingHoldsPressThenEmits`, `testSecondFingerDuringStrokeArmingBecomesGesture`, `testPinchDuringStrokeArmingDrawsNoAtom` (draw tool active, empty molecule, pinch → no atom drawn, camera zooms), plus the arming cleanup/delivery slots `testCancelDuringStrokeArmingEmitsNothing`, `testEndDuringStrokeArmingEmitsPressRelease`, `testBeginDuringStrokeArmingFormsGesture`, and the updated stroke/palm/resting/cancel slots; `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8`; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 green. — **Verified**: touchnavigationtest = 29 passed / 1 skipped (dpr), full ctest = 49/49 passed. The `AVOGADRO_TEST_NOPLUGIN` build compiles `drawtool.cpp`/`placement.cpp` directly into the test (added to the touchnavigation CMake block). The fix is a policy decision (design D2 amendment) and does not modify any tool.

[OpenSpec 19] 5.6 Widen the stroke-arming window so a pinch cannot draw an atom on the P52 (via /opsx-apply). Device evidence (author-confirmed fresh installer, run 42656894181 = c5e33bf39, 2026-11-10): with the 50ms window a pinch with the draw tool active STILL drew atoms — the window elapsed while finger 1 was still moving toward the pinch (human finger-planting commonly takes 150–400ms), the press reached the draw tool, and finger 2 was then blacklisted. Raise `kTouchStrokeArmMs` from 50ms to ~250ms (design D2 amendment): covers typical pinch planting; the cost is a touch-only stroke-start ink delay (mouse unaffected, bond-draw strokes tolerate it, taps unchanged). If the 5.2 re-record still shows atoms drawn, escalate to the recovery policy recorded in D2 (synthesized release + undo of the tool's release command; verified mechanic: DrawTool press mutates the live molecule directly at drawtool.cpp:291–296 and its AddAtomDrawCommand exists only at release, drawtool.cpp:607–615). — Verify: `kTouchStrokeArmMs` updated and the arming tests' timestamps follow the named constant (no hardcoded 50); `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8`; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` green; 5.2 pinch re-recorded on the P52 passing with the draw tool active. — **Code implemented (2026-11-10)**: `kTouchStrokeArmMs` raised 50ms → 250ms (glwidget_touch_p.h:30); all arming test timestamps follow the named constant (no hardcoded 50); `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8` succeeds; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed. **Deferred (external)**: the 5.2 pinch re-record on the author's P52 remains pending (cannot be performed on this runner).

[OpenSpec 20] 5.7 Implement the three-finger orbit gesture (via /opsx-apply) — pulled into this change by explicit user decision (2026-11-10): two-finger horizontal movement must PAN (the P52 "twist" was gesture non-formation degrading to the one-finger rotate fallback; pan wiring verified correct at glwidget.cpp:3509), and rotation moves to three fingers. A third live point arriving while the two-finger GESTURE is in flight promotes the gesture to a THREE-FINGER ORBIT: the centroid delta of the three points drives `Navigate::rotate(widget, center, dx, dy)` with the navigate tool's left-drag mapping (navigatetool.cpp:241); a touch event beginning with ≥3 points goes straight to the orbit; the orbit replaces the pinch (zoom/pan deltas stop at promotion); the gesture ends when any of the three original ids lifts (camera holds, no tool events); a third point during a single-finger STROKE remains second-class (palm rejection unchanged); the broken-pair rule is unchanged (no replenishment after a break). Spec delta: "Three fingers orbit the camera" requirement + scenarios; second-class requirement amended with the promotion exception. — Verify: new unit slots (three-point begin → orbit with camera rotate delta; promotion from pinch → orbit; orbit end holds camera; third-finger-during-stroke still blacklisted; orbit with draw tool active draws no atom) pass under xvfb; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` green; MSVC-safe constructs (D8); 5.2 orbit scenario re-recorded on the P52. — **Code implemented (2026-11-10)**: `TouchState` gains orbit state (m_orbit/m_gestureId3/m_lastOrbitCentroid, glwidget_touch_p.h) and `TouchResult` gains orbitFrom/orbitTo; onBegin (≥3 points straight to orbit; a third point during a live pinch promotes), onUpdate (orbit branch drives the three-point centroid; pinch → orbit promotion; pinch deltas stop), onEnd/onCancel reset orbit state; GLWidget::touchEvent dispatches `Navigate::rotate(this, center(), dx*dpr, dy*dpr)` before zoom/pan (glwidget.cpp). New unit slots `testThreePointBeginGoesToOrbit`, `testThirdFingerPromotesPinchToOrbit`, `testOrbitEndHoldsCamera`, `testThirdFingerDuringStrokeStillBlacklisted`, `testOrbitWithDrawToolActiveDrawsNoAtom`; touchnavigationtest = 34 passed / 1 skipped (dpr); `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed. **Deferred (external)**: the 5.2 orbit re-record on the author's P52 remains pending. — **Platform gate (Microsoft-documented, 2026-11-10)**: on Windows 11 the OS setting 'Bluetooth & devices > Touch > Three- and four-finger touch gestures' (default On) delivers three/four-finger touches to the SHELL (task switcher), and applications cannot receive them; set Off, applications receive them and the system does not ('Three-finger and four-finger touch interactions don't work in Windows apps', learn.microsoft.com troubleshoot/win32; 'Touch interactions developer guide'). The P52 report of the gesture switching apps is this documented preemption — present on every build, not a defect in the orbit code, and the resulting `TouchCancel` is already handled (D9: camera holds). App-level suppression is rejected (design D11): DirectManipulation `SetContact` claims contacts away from the WM_POINTER stream (starving the one/two-finger pipeline); the registry `TouchGestureSetting` + `SystemParametersInfo(SPI_SETGESTURE)` path is community-documented only and flips a GLOBAL per-user setting. Mitigation: task 5.8 (dialog guidance + deep link to `ms-settings:devices-touch`). Re-record split: with the OS setting On → the task switch is expected OS behavior (record as OS behavior, not failure); with the OS setting Off → the orbit must engage (the pass condition).

[OpenSpec 21] 5.8 Windows three-finger gate guidance (via /opsx-apply): Windows 11 routes 3/4-finger touches to the shell while the OS setting 'Three- and four-finger touch gestures' is On (its default; design D11), so the orbit is inert on stock Windows regardless of the app's orbit toggle. Windows-only guidance in `TouchSettingsDialog` (no main-window code): a read-only hint naming the OS setting and an "Open Windows touch settings…" push button deep-linking `ms-settings:devices-touch` via `QDesktopServices::openUrl`; both absent on non-Windows platforms. Plus a discoverable preemption signal: when a touch session that has observed ≥3 contacts ends in `QEvent::TouchCancel` (the shell-claim signature), `GLWidget` emits `touchGesturePreempted()` at most once per run — no modal dialogs, no tool changes (D5), strokes unaffected. — Verify: new unit slots — the dialog's guidance row is present on Windows builds (skipped elsewhere) and `touchGesturePreempted()` fires exactly once for a 3-contact session cancelled by TouchCancel and never for ordinary cancels; `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest dialogsmoketest -j8`; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` green; Windows installer workflow passes (D8). — **Code implemented (2026-11-10)**: `GLWidget` gains signal `touchGesturePreempted()` (glwidget.h Q_SIGNALS) and `GLWidgetPrivate` tracks `m_touchSessionMaxContacts` (max contacts delivered per touch session) plus a once-per-run latch `m_touchPreemptedNotified` — a session that observed >= 3 contacts and ends in `QEvent::TouchCancel` (the Windows 11 shell-claim signature, D11) emits exactly once; ordinary cancels and normal TouchEnd never fire it; per-widget, no static state (D6). `TouchSettingsDialog` gains a Windows-only guidance row (`#ifdef Q_OS_WIN`): a word-wrapped label naming the OS setting (objectName `touchWindowsGuidanceLabel`) and an "Open Windows touch settings..." push button (`touchWindowsSettingsButton`) deep-linking `ms-settings:devices-touch` via `QDesktopServices::openUrl`; both absent on non-Windows. New slots: `touchnavigationtest::testTouchGesturePreemptedFiresOnceForShellClaim` (3-contact session ending in TouchEnd does not notify; 3-contact + TouchCancel notifies exactly once; latch holds on a second preemption), `testOrdinaryCancelDoesNotNotifyPreemption` (2-contact cancel never notifies), `dialogsmoketest::touchSettingsDialogWindowsGuidance` (guidance row present on Windows builds, QSKIP elsewhere). touchnavigationtest = 42 passed / 1 skipped (dpr); full `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed. **Deferred (external)**: Windows installer (D8) verification via the auto-triggered workflow on push. — **Note (2026-11-10)**: the guidance surface moves to the Settings > Configure Avogadro > General tab by task 6.3 (user decision); the guidance logic (label + ms-settings deep link + `touchGesturePreempted()` latch) is unchanged and moves with the widget. Touch settings panel (scope added by user decision, 2026-11-10; design D10)

[OpenSpec 22] 6.1 Settings plumbing (via /opsx-apply): `TouchState` gains `armMs` and `orbitEnabled` constructor parameters defaulting to the named constants (slop is already a parameter, so existing tests are untouched); `GLWidget` caches the three values (defaults `kTouchStrokeArmMs`/`kTouchSlopLogicalPx`/true), loads them in `GLWidget::readSettings(QSettings&)` under keys `touchStrokeArmMs`/`touchSlopPx`/`touchOrbitEnabled` with defaults and clamp-on-read (the existing `projection` pattern), and consumes them at `touchEvent` dispatch; live application without restart; orbit-disabled behavior per D10 (a third point during a gesture stays second-class; a ≥3-point begin forms a pinch from the first two). — Verify: new unit slots (non-default `armMs` alters arming timing; `orbitEnabled=false` keeps the pinch and rejects promotion; ≥3-point begin with orbit off forms a pinch from the first two); `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8`; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` green. — **Code implemented (2026-11-10)**: `TouchState(double slopLogicalPx, qint64 armMs = kTouchStrokeArmMs, bool orbitEnabled = true)` with a `configure()` method; `GLWidgetPrivate` caches `m_touchStrokeArmMs`/`m_touchSlopPx`/`m_touchOrbitEnabled` and applies them via `applyTouchSettings()`; `GLWidget::readSettings`/`writeSettings` persist the three keys with `qBound` clamping to the documented ranges (`kTouchStrokeArmMsMin/Max`, `kTouchSlopLogicalPxMin/Max`); orbit promotions gated on `m_orbitEnabled` (a ≥3-point begin with orbit off forms a pinch from the first two); public `GLWidget::setTouchSettings()` for the panel's live apply. New unit slots `testNonDefaultArmMsAltersArmingTiming`, `testOrbitDisabledKeepsPinchAndRejectsPromotion`, `testThreePointBeginWithOrbitOffFormsPinchFromFirstTwo`; touchnavigationtest = 37 passed / 1 skipped (dpr); `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed.

[OpenSpec 23] 6.2 Settings panel UI (via /opsx-apply): a small modeless `TouchSettingsDialog` (`libavogadro/src/touchsettingsdialog.{h,cpp}`) — arming-window spin box (50–1000 ms, default `kTouchStrokeArmMs`), slop spin box (4–40 logical px, default `kTouchSlopLogicalPx`), orbit checkbox (default on), reset-to-defaults button; writes the QSettings keys from 6.1 and live-applies to active views; mounted as "Settings → Touch Interaction…" through the standard extension menu machinery (the constraints/symmetry dialog pattern), no main-window code. MSVC-safe plain widgets (D8). — Verify: headless build succeeds and a unit/smoke slot constructs the dialog, loads, clamps an out-of-range value, saves, and resets to defaults; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` green; Windows installer workflow passes (D8). — **Code implemented (2026-11-10)**: `libavogadro/src/touchsettingsdialog.{h,cpp}` (A_EXPORT QDialog, injected `QSettings*` ctor param, three controls + reset, `applyAndPersist()` live-apply slot connected to valueChanged/toggled, getters `armMs()/slopPx()/orbitEnabled()`); `libavogadro/src/extensions/touchsettingsextension.{h,cpp}` mounted via `avogadro_plugin_nogl(touchsettingsextension ...)` with `menuPath` = `tr("Se&ttings")` (the root Settings menu title is `Se&ttings`, mnemonic on the second 't' — `addActionsToMenu` matches by exact string equality); added to `libavogadro_SRCS`/`HDRS`/`MOC_HDRS`. Storage clarification (design D10): the three touch keys are app-GLOBAL at the root of QSettings — `GLWidget::readSettings` reads them from a fresh default-constructed `QSettings` (this method is positioned inside the per-view `view/<i>` array), and the touch `setValue` lines were removed from `writeSettings` (the dialog is the sole writer). New slots: `dialogsmoketest::touchSettingsDialogLoadsClampsSavesResets` (injected ini-backed QSettings; clamps 5000→1000 ms / 100→40 px; reset writes the constants 250/10/true) and `touchnavigationtest::testDialogLiveAppliesOrbitDisabled` (dialog live-applies orbit=off to the widget; a 3-point begin forms a pinch, not an orbit, so moving only the third point leaves the camera unchanged). touchnavigationtest = 40 passed / 1 skipped (dpr); dialogsmoketest = 14 passed; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed. **Windows installer (D8) verified**: run 42784147658 (= 6c890f441) completed **success** — both `build-installer` jobs (installer + tests) passed, so the dialog and extension compile and run green under MSVC; that artifact is the first shipped build containing the settings menu. **Author device report (2026-11-10)**: no menu entry observed under Settings — the tested binary (c5e33bf39) predates the extension (see 5.2); if the menu is still absent on the run-42784147658 artifact, it is a plugin-discovery/dependency-closure defect to fix via /opsx-apply. — **ROOT CAUSE FOUND (loader-level, 2026-11-10, superseded by task 6.3)**: the menu absence is build-independent — `touchsettingsextension.h` ships no plugin factory. Every working extension carries a `XxxExtensionFactory : public QObject, public PluginFactory` with `Q_OBJECT`, `Q_INTERFACES(Avogadro::PluginFactory)`, `Q_PLUGIN_METADATA(IID "net.sourceforge.avogadro.pluginfactory/1.5")`, and `AVOGADRO_EXTENSION_FACTORY(Xxx)` (pattern: symmetryextension.h:104-111; 34/34 extensions have it), while `avogadro_plugin_nogl` (libavogadro/CMakeLists.txt:25) only creates the MODULE target and generates no metadata. `PluginManager` (pluginmanager.cpp:784-791) loads each DLL via `QPluginLoader::instance()` then `qobject_cast<PluginFactory *>` — the cast fails for a factory-less DLL, so the extension is never constructed and no action is ever mounted (the earlier menuPath/wiring verification was correct but unreachable). User decision: relocate the UI into the Configure dialog (6.3) and RETIRE the extension plugin rather than repair it (the factory fix is the recorded rejected alternative).

[OpenSpec 24] 6.3 Relocate the touch settings into Settings > Configure Avogadro > General tab (via /opsx-apply; user decision 2026-11-10). The Configure dialog is `avogadro/src/settingsdialog.{h,cpp,ui}` (`SettingsDialog`, opened by `MainWindow::showSettingsDialog()`); its General tab hosts a "General" QGroupBox (quality/fog controls) — add a "Touch" section/group there hosting the touch controls. Rework `TouchSettingsDialog` (`libavogadro/src/touchsettingsdialog.{h,cpp}`) into an embeddable QWidget-based panel keeping: the three behavior controls (arming window spin box, slop spin box, orbit checkbox), the reset-to-defaults button, injected-`QSettings` persistence (app-global root keys per D10, widget is sole writer), live application via `GLWidget::setTouchSettings`, and the Windows-only guidance row + `ms-settings:devices-touch` deep link (5.8/D11) unchanged. Retire `libavogadro/src/extensions/touchsettingsextension.{h,cpp}` and its CMake/plugin registration (the broken mounting; factory-fix recorded as rejected alternative). No tool modifications (D5); MSVC-safe plain widgets (D8). — Verify: headless build succeeds; `dialogsmoketest` slots reworked to the embedded panel — load, clamp an out-of-range value, save, reset to defaults, guidance row present on Windows builds (QSKIP elsewhere); `touchnavigationtest::testDialogLiveAppliesOrbitDisabled` reworked to the panel's live-apply (orbit-disabled propagates to `GLWidget::setTouchSettings`; 3-point begin forms a pinch, not an orbit); `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest dialogsmoketest -j8`; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49; Windows installer workflow passes (D8). — **Code implemented (2026-11-10)**: `TouchSettingsDialog` reworked from a modeless `QDialog` into an embeddable `QWidget` panel (base `QWidget`, no OK/Cancel button box, zero-margin layout so it nests cleanly); the three behavior controls + reset button + injected-`QSettings` persistence + live-apply + Windows-only guidance row/`ms-settings:devices-touch` deep link (5.8/D11) are all preserved unchanged. `avogadro/src/settingsdialog.ui` gains a "Touch" QGroupBox in the General tab hosting the panel; `SettingsDialog` (settingsdialog.{h,cpp}) constructs the panel, adds it to `ui.touchGroupBoxLayout`, calls `loadSettings()` on open, and reloads it on Reject (live-apply means an edit is already persisted, but a Cancel re-syncs the controls). The broken `touchsettingsextension` plugin is RETIRED: `avogadro_plugin_nogl(touchsettingsextension ...)` removed from extensions/CMakeLists.txt and the `touchsettingsextension.{h,cpp}` files deleted (the factory-less DLL could never mount — task 6.2 root cause). New slot `dialogsmoketest::touchSettingsDialogEmbedsAsWidget` (a QWidget, not a QDialog; 2 spin boxes + 1 checkbox; added to a parent layout); existing `touchSettingsDialogLoadsClampsSavesResets`/`touchSettingsDialogWindowsGuidance` and `touchnavigationtest::testDialogLiveAppliesOrbitDisabled` pass against the reworked panel. touchnavigationtest = 42 passed / 1 skipped (dpr); dialogsmoketest = 15 passed; `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed. **Deferred (external)**: Windows installer (D8) verification via the auto-triggered workflow on push.

findingGroups.title: Touch input pipeline
findings: Single-finger touch reaches tools as synthesized mouse events with tap/click parity, jitter swallowing, and one-finger rotate preserved through the navigate fallback — unit-tested in touchnavigationtest and confirmed on the P52.
Two-finger pinch zoom and centroid pan drive the camera at the widget level before tool dispatch; three-finger orbit uses the navigate drag mapping — confirmed working on device.

Extra fingers are second-class (palm rejection, resting-finger-never-wakes, broken-pair no-replenish), with a committed-stroke recovery that undoes an editing tool's partial mutation when a second finger lands late.

findingGroups.title: Touch settings panel
findings: The three touch controls (arming window, slop, orbit) live in Settings > Configure Avogadro > General as an embeddable QWidget panel, persisted app-globally via QSettings with clamp-on-read and live apply.
The broken factory-less extension plugin was retired and replaced by the embeddable panel; Windows-only guidance + ms-settings deep link added.

findingGroups.title: P52 pinch-draws-atom fix
findings: Root cause was dual-stream delivery: Windows posts the primary touch contact as QTouchEvent (via WM_POINTER, handled by the pipeline) AND as OS-synthesized legacy WM_MOUSE* that Qt forwards as real QMouseEvents by default, bypassing WA_AcceptTouchEvents and every touch setting.

Fix: Windows-only `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=windows:nomousefromtouch` injection in main.cpp, guarded to respect explicit -platform/--platform and existing windows:* values; stops the OS mouse stream and re-enables Qt synthesis for non-touch widgets.
Author confirmed on the ThinkPad P52 that the touch feature works — 'just pass the last tasks. the feature works'.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.

[OpenSpec 17] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition(), which in Qt 6 widget delivery equals globalPosition() (qguiapplication.cpp sets scenePosition = globalPosition; QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal, never scenePosition), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the widget's GLOBAL origin (toolbar/dock chrome plus the window's on-screen position); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level and a (0,0)-positioned parent makes mapTo(window) coincide with mapToGlobal. Pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget AND moves the parent to a non-zero global position so the test discriminates mapToGlobal from mapTo(window). (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. findingGroups.title: Touch input pipeline
findings: Single-finger touch reaches tools as synthesized mouse events with tap/click parity, jitter swallowing, and one-finger rotate preserved through the navigate fallback — unit-tested in touchnavigationtest and confirmed on the P52.
Two-finger pinch zoom and centroid pan drive the camera at the widget level before tool dispatch; three-finger orbit uses the navigate drag mapping — confirmed working on device.

Extra fingers are second-class (palm rejection, resting-finger-never-wakes, broken-pair no-replenish), with a committed-stroke recovery that undoes an editing tool's partial mutation when a second finger lands late.

findingGroups.title: Touch settings panel
findings: The three touch controls (arming window, slop, orbit) live in Settings > Configure Avogadro > General as an embeddable QWidget panel, persisted app-globally via QSettings with clamp-on-read and live apply.
The broken factory-less extension plugin was retired and replaced by the embeddable panel; Windows-only guidance + ms-settings deep link added.

findingGroups.title: P52 pinch-draws-atom fix
findings: Root cause was dual-stream delivery: Windows posts the primary touch contact as QTouchEvent (via WM_POINTER, handled by the pipeline) AND as OS-synthesized legacy WM_MOUSE* that Qt forwards as real QMouseEvents by default, bypassing WA_AcceptTouchEvents and every touch setting.

Fix: Windows-only `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=windows:nomousefromtouch` injection in main.cpp, guarded to respect explicit -platform/--platform and existing windows:* values; stops the OS mouse stream and re-enables Qt synthesis for non-touch widgets.
Author confirmed on the ThinkPad P52 that the touch feature works — 'just pass the last tasks. the feature works'.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-touch-navigation --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

8. Every mirrored GLLA task is complete (the GLLA task list shows no open tasks), so GLLA's pending-task gate does not refuse completion.

findingGroups.title: Touch input pipeline
findings: Single-finger touch reaches tools as synthesized mouse events with tap/click parity, jitter swallowing, and one-finger rotate preserved through the navigate fallback — unit-tested in touchnavigationtest and confirmed on the P52.
Two-finger pinch zoom and centroid pan drive the camera at the widget level before tool dispatch; three-finger orbit uses the navigate drag mapping — confirmed working on device.

Extra fingers are second-class (palm rejection, resting-finger-never-wakes, broken-pair no-replenish), with a committed-stroke recovery that undoes an editing tool's partial mutation when a second finger lands late.

findingGroups.title: Touch settings panel
findings: The three touch controls (arming window, slop, orbit) live in Settings > Configure Avogadro > General as an embeddable QWidget panel, persisted app-globally via QSettings with clamp-on-read and live apply.
The broken factory-less extension plugin was retired and replaced by the embeddable panel; Windows-only guidance + ms-settings deep link added.

findingGroups.title: P52 pinch-draws-atom fix
findings: Root cause was dual-stream delivery: Windows posts the primary touch contact as QTouchEvent (via WM_POINTER, handled by the pipeline) AND as OS-synthesized legacy WM_MOUSE* that Qt forwards as real QMouseEvents by default, bypassing WA_AcceptTouchEvents and every touch setting.

Fix: Windows-only `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=windows:nomousefromtouch` injection in main.cpp, guarded to respect explicit -platform/--platform and existing windows:* values; stops the OS mouse stream and re-enables Qt synthesis for non-touch widgets.
Author confirmed on the ThinkPad P52 that the touch feature works — 'just pass the last tasks. the feature works'.
